name: Warsaw Rising Museum
description: A museum in a former tram power station about the 1944 Warsaw Uprising against the German occupation, told through objects, film and sound.

name: Palace of Culture and Science
places: Congress Hall, Palace of Culture and Science
description: A Stalin-era skyscraper given to Warsaw by the Soviet Union in the 1950s, with theatres, a congress hall and a viewing terrace.

name: Royal Castle
description: The Polish kings’ castle, blown up in 1944 and rebuilt in the 1970s, and Castle Square in front with Sigismund’s Column.

name: Old Town Market Square
description: The main square of the Old Town, destroyed in 1944 and rebuilt after the war from old paintings, drawings and photographs.

name: Wilanów Palace
description: A baroque palace built for King Jan III Sobieski in the late 17th century, with formal gardens. Its rooms are now a museum.

name: Łazienki Palace
places: Palace on the Isle, Łazienki Park
description: A large royal park with a classical palace standing in a lake, built for Poland’s last king in the 18th century.

name: Maria Skłodowska-Curie Museum
description: A small museum in the New Town house where Marie Curie was born in 1867, about her life and her work on radioactivity.

name: Constitution Square
description: A large square at the heart of the MDM housing district, built in the early 1950s in the socialist realist style, with reliefs of workers.

name: Miła 18
description: A grassy mound and memorial stone over the bunker where leaders of the 1943 Warsaw Ghetto Uprising died.

name: Warsaw Ghetto wall fragment
description: One of the few surviving stretches of the wall that enclosed the Warsaw Ghetto, in a courtyard off Sienna Street, with memorial plaques.

name: Warsaw Zoo
description: The city zoo on the east bank of the Vistula. The director’s villa inside, where Jews were hidden during the war, is open to visitors.
